Timing

Your audience has a deadline

Pregnancy lasts months, not years. A follower who isn’t ready to apply this week may not need you at all by next season, and today there is nothing in between to keep her close.

Your calendar

Applications arrive cold

Someone can go from one reel to an application with no idea how you work. You find out on the call whether she’s ready, and every unready call costs you clinical time.

Reach

Growth tied to the next reel

Your reels travel, but each view is a one-off. Who sees your coaching depends on how this week’s content does, with no steady way to reach new expecting moms every day.

Expecting moms already trust you enough to save and share your posts. The missing piece is a small, first thing of yours to say yes to.

My recommendation

A $17 live class, “Eat With Confidence”, built on your practical approach

You don’t have a low-ticket product yet, so the class itself should be paid. A $17 seat earns from the first sale and helps pay for the ads, a Balanced Pregnancy Kitchen Kit on the thank-you page adds to it, and your coaching application moves to the replay page, so applications come from moms who have already seen you teach.

RD & CDCES

Sound familiar?

So much food advice in pregnancy. So little of it practical.

  • Every app, forum and relative has a different list of what to eat and what to avoid.
  • You know a balanced plate matters, but on a tired Tuesday night it’s hard to know what that looks like.
  • Snacks, cravings and eating out feel like guesswork.
  • You want to walk into your next appointment with good questions, not a search history.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover live

The balanced pregnancy plate

A simple, flexible way to build meals with protein, fibre-rich carbs, healthy fats and colour, without counting or strict rules.

Snacks that actually work

How to pair foods for snacks that keep you satisfied, with easy options for home, work and on the go.

Gestational diabetes, explained simply

An educational overview of what GD is, why it’s screened for, and how dietitians generally approach meals. Your own plan always comes from your care team.

Eating out and busy days

How to apply the plate idea to restaurants, takeout and the nights you don’t want to cook.

Questions for your care team

The nutrition questions worth bringing to your next appointment, so you leave with answers that fit you.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Why is it $17 and not free?

Because people who invest, even a little, show up and use what they learn. I want a room of moms ready to try one practical change.

Is this medical advice?

No. The class is general nutrition education. It doesn’t replace your doctor, midwife or care team, and it isn’t individual medical nutrition therapy. Please talk to your care team about your own pregnancy.

Is the class about gestational diabetes?

Partly. It covers practical pregnancy nutrition for any expecting mom, with an educational section on GD basics. If you’ve been given a plan by your care team, keep following it and bring your questions to them.

Is this a diet?

No. There’s no restriction and no counting. It’s about building balanced, satisfying meals that fit real life.

What if I can’t make it live?

Save your seat anyway. Every seat includes the full replay.

Will you talk about coaching at the end?

For the last few minutes I’ll share how to apply for 1:1 nutrition coaching, for anyone who wants personal support. Everything before that is yours to use either way.

The thought I hear most after class: “This was so helpful. I’ll figure out the rest myself.”

That’s what 1:1 nutrition coaching is for: a dietitian in your corner who looks at your real meals and routines, works alongside your care team, and adjusts with you as your pregnancy goes on.

Script 1 · “Conflicting advice”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Expecting moms get more food advice than almost anyone. Here’s how a prenatal dietitian keeps it simple.”

Body

“Every app and every relative has a different list. What I teach instead is one flexible plate: some protein, some fibre-rich carbs, some healthy fat, some colour. That’s the starting point, and a care team helps tailor it from there.”

CTA

“I’m teaching it live in Eat With Confidence. Seats are $17, replay included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera in your kitchen, white top, captions on, end card “Educational content, not medical advice”. No blood sugar numbers, weight talk or “you have GD” language.

Script 2 · “Three-step plate”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“This is how a dietitian builds a balanced pregnancy plate in three steps.”

Body

“Step one, pick a protein. Step two, add a fibre-rich carb. Step three, finish with veg or fruit and a healthy fat. No counting, no strict rules. I’ll show you three real plates for busy days.”

CTA

“Learn it live with me for $17. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: overhead, building one bowl in three moves with on-screen text for each step. Same feel as your current reels.
